content:
sara-ml: heads up — brought up sylph (dense-1024) on staging for a quick semantic recall sweep. shorttail recall@10 dropped ~6.5% vs baseline on our short-query cohort.
cheng: do you have the exact eval vectorization settings? cosine or l2?
sara-ml: cosine, normalization on, whitening OFF. microbatch=8, kvcache disabled (probe-only). used int8-perchannel quant.
tara: hmm int8-perchannel could shift scale. any per-dim clamp used?
sara-ml: we used clamp=0.02 (same as the baseline config). ran a tiny ablation: float32 sylph vs int8-perchannel produced delta: +0.2 vs baseline, int8 -6.7.
mike: is the baseline the older albatross-embed-1024?
sara-ml: yeah baseline=albatross-v2-1024 float32. small queries = length < 16 tokens.
jamie: can you paste the eval snippet (recall by bucket)?
sara-ml: sure:
```
bucket: short (<16) recall@10
- baseline albatross float32: 0.842
- sylph float32: 0.845
- sylph int8-perchannel: 0.778
overall recall@10 shift: -0.064
```
cheng: wild — int8 regression that big suggests quant noise on short sequences (KV cache eviction not relevant here). did you try per-channel zero-point vs symmetric quant?
sara-ml: symmetric per-channel (no zero point). we can try asymmetric quickly.
mike: also check microbatching effect — we saw microbatch <-> rounding nondeterminism in earlier int4 experiments. can you run microbatch=1?
sara-ml: queued microbatch=1 job now. eval-bot: queued job 87321: sylph int8-perchannel microbatch=1 asymmetric=false whitening=off. results ETA ~12m.
jamie: also run a cosine vs l2 parity check — sometimes similarity metric amplifies small scale changes.
sara-ml: added l2 run to queue.
ops-bot: FYI staging pool has 2x sylph int8 nodes rolling. no traffic routing yet.
sara-ml: quick note: embedding norm distribution looked weird for int8 — mean norm 1.12 vs 0.98 baseline. slacking a small histogram in a sec.
(sara-ml uploads: sylph_int8_norm_hist.png)
cheng: can you rerun with whitening ON? we saw whitening recover shorttail in other models.
sara-ml: trying whitening=on, microbatch=1, asymmetric quant. eval-bot: queued job 87322: sylph int8-perchannel microbatch=1 asymmetric=true whitening=on. results ETA ~14m.
mike: if whitening fixes it we should add auto-whitening to onboard checklist for int8 variants.
jamie: also check neighborhood stability: top-5 neighbors overlap between float32 and int8 for short queries.
sara-ml: added neighbor-overlap check.
eval-bot: job 87321 complete — microbatch=1 asymmetric=false whitening=off: recall@10 = 0.781 (short). top5 overlap with float32 = 0.69.
sara-ml: interim: microbatch didn't help much, overlap low.
eval-bot: job 87322 complete — asymmetric=true whitening=on: recall@10 = 0.835 (short). top5 overlap with float32 = 0.92.
jamie: that's a big recovery. looks like whitening + asymmetric quant is the combo.
cheng: can you run a quick clustering sanity (kmeans k=200) on a 10k subset to check silhouette shift?
sara-ml: running kmeans now. ops-bot: staging deploy paused for sylph-int8 until we confirm quant config.
mike: capture config in the model card and flag int8-asymmetric+whitening as recommended for sylph.
sara-ml: will update model card and open a tiny PR to onboard checklist. linking eval dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/evals/87321-87322
jamie: nice find — thanks for the fast triage :thumbsup:
sara-ml: np. taking next steps: run full recall sweep with whitening+asymm, add unit test for neighbor-overlap >=0.9 for short cohort. will post results here.
(THREAD END)
